key_insight: Adding a monolayer graphene front contact to AlInN/Si solar cells improves charge collection and boosts efficiency without significantly changing open-circuit voltage.
engineering_relevance: Graphene offers a low-temperature, transparent conductive contact that can enhance nitride-on-silicon photovoltaic device performance and is compatible with practical fabrication workflows.
method: Fabricated AlxIn1-xN solar cells on p-type Si(100) with a thin amorphous-Si buffer layer.
Studied three Al compositions: x = 0.22, 0.35, and 0.43.
Transferred a monolayer graphene film onto the front surface and compared devices with/without graphene under dark and illuminated conditions.
evidence_signal: Across all three compositions, the graphene-coated devices showed higher short-circuit current density, fill factor, and power conversion efficiency, while open-circuit voltage stayed largely unchanged.
watch_item: The transfer quality and long-term stability of the graphene contact may be critical for maintaining the observed performance gains in scalable device manufacturing.
paper_title: Enhancement of nitride-based solar cells using graphene as transparent contact layer
